title: How We Got the Name 'Spider Tales'
source: Barker & Sinclair, West African Folk-Tales (1917), tale I
lesson: Cleverness can win what strength cannot.
lines: Why are so many African stories called Anansi stories? Because of one clever spider. Every story belonged to Nyankupon, the sky chief.
Anansi wanted them. Fine, said Nyankupon. Bring me a jar of live bees, a boa constrictor, and a tiger.
Anansi took a jar to the bees, and argued with himself. They can't fill it. Yes, they can! The bees buzzed out. We can! In they flew. Lid on!
Next, a long stick for the boa. He's not as long as this. Yes, he is! The proud boa stretched out to be measured, and Anansi tied him to the stick.
Then Anansi tied a cloth over one eye, and sang about wonders.
The tiger begged: Do mine too!
Nyankupon was amazed, and from then on, the old tales were Anansi tales. Cleverness can win what strength cannot.
Next time: Anansi tries to keep all the world's wisdom in one pot. Follow so you don't miss it!
